# The Book of Octads <note>original: "Atthakavagga"</note>

836. <note>Māgandiya speaks:</note> "If you do not desire such a jewel, this woman sought after by many lords of men, then what kind of view, what way of life based on moral habits and vows, and what kind of future rebirth do you proclaim?"

837. <note>The Blessed One <gloss>Bhagavā</gloss> speaks:</note> "O Māgandiya, for such a one <note>an awakened person</note> there is no 'I say this' based on things taken up after judging among various teachings. Looking among different views but not grasping them, and searching for inward peace <note>original: "ajjhattasanti"</note>, I saw what is not seen by others."

838. <note>Māgandiya speaks:</note> "Those systems that have been judged and formulated, O Sage, you say you do not grasp them. As for this matter you call 'inward peace', how is that proclaimed by the wise?"

839. <note>The Blessed One speaks:</note> "One does not say there is purity by means of views, or by what is heard, or by knowledge, Māgandiya. Nor does one find purity by means of moral habits and vows. Yet, it is not by the absence of views, the absence of hearing, the absence of knowledge, or the absence of habits and vows that one is purified. Having let go of these without grasping them, being at peace and independent, one would not long for becoming <note>continued existence</note>."

840. <note>Māgandiya speaks:</note> "If you truly say there is no purification by means of views, or by what is heard, or by knowledge, or even by moral habits and vows...

<summary>A dialogue between Māgandiya and the Buddha regarding the nature of spiritual purity and the rejection of dogmatic views. The Buddha explains that true inward peace comes from not grasping at rituals, knowledge, or specific philosophical systems.</summary>
<keywords>Māgandiya, Buddha, purification, inward peace, views, moral habits, vows, Atthakavagga</keywords>
